newsitem.title: FINLAND: FOCUS - Metsa-Serla warning hits forestries.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Metsa-Serla warning hits forestries.

text.p: Finnish forestry stocks were hit on Tuesday when Metsa-Serla Oy, the country's third largest pulp and paper company, warned it expected to make a loss in May-December.

The company, which last year crested a cyclical boom in the industry to report bumper profits, said it would still be in the black for full-year 1996 thanks to a 318 million markka ($70.4 million) January-April profit.
But it largely blamed a surprisingly sharp fall in pulp prices and particularly fine paper products for the forecast loss. It also listed other more incidental factors.

Metsa-Serla said it would announce details of action to be taken to improve its competitiveness when it publishes its interim report for January-August on October 17, but a company official declined to elaborate on Tuesday.
"The biggest impact is indeed from fine paper prices," Metsa-Serla senior vice president Hannu Anttila told Reuters.

Metsa-Serla's warning took already weak forestry shares down, but with its rivals it later trimmed losses as already bearish analysts targeted the one-off elements in its statement, limiting the damage especially to other companies.

In late trading the Helsinki forestry index stood down around two percent at 2,133.27, having earlier fallen to around 2,115. Metsa-Serla was down 0.70 markka or over two percent at 31.00, off a 30.00 markka low.

Metsa-Serla said several development projects and investments would lead to non-recurring expenditure of around 300 million markka, referring to restructuring at its recent German acquisition MD Papier, and the start-up of a new mill.
"It's probably more than just problems in the market," said Dennis Christie at Kleinwort Benson in London. "I think most people will have to revise their forecasts down quite dramatically."

Nine analysts polled by Reuters in June had pointed to a full-year profit of, on average, around 800 million markka for Metsa-Serla, but the range then was already very wide at 130-1,106 million markka.
Metsa-Serla said prospects for its other business operations were in line with the targets set for the year.
Anna-Maija Pirskanen at Merita Securities, said she would lower her 1996 forecast for Metsa-Serla, but not for other forestry groups.
"We have such a negative view at forestries in general, that we don't need to revise forecasts for other companies," she said, adding Merita has an underweight recommendation on forestries.
But although she saw one-off factors mainly behind Metsa-Serla's warning, she said it also underlined reasons for caution in the forestry sector.
"This is mainly due to one-off factors, but we cannot deny that capacity ratios and paper prices have also declined," she said. "It seems that the recovery will be somewhat delayed."

Metsa-Serla's Anttila said the warning had been forced by the very low depths ploughed by fine paper prices before they started to rise again. He declined to say if Metsa-Serla was loss-making at current price levels.
"The turn has happened but it came at such a low level ... prices are still very unsatisfactory," he said. "The low level of the bottom price was really a surprise."
In 1995, Metsa-Serla posted a 1.91 billion markka profit after financial items, up from 786 million in 1994. ($1=4.52 Markka)
